---
title: JupyterLite
---

JupyterLite is a browser-based version of Jupyter Notebook / Jupyter Lab. The official documentation can be found [here](https://jupyterlite.readthedocs.io/en/stable/). 

JupyterLite offers a minimal setup way of running Python, similar to Google Colab but without needing a Google account. 

The JupyterLite instance below opens a short, self-contained sequence-analysis
notebook demonstrating Biopython, NumPy, pandas, and Matplotlib. The first run
may take a little while because the packages are downloaded into the browser;
later runs can reuse the browser's cache.

For many tasks this is essentially a full fledged Python notebook interface and can for example be used for tasks requiring packages such as 

- [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/stable/): Core plotting library that can be used to make practically any type of scientific plot.
- [NumPy](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/): Provides efficient numerical calculations with multidimensional arrays.
- [SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/): Supplies algorithms for scientific computing, including optimization, integration, interpolation, and statistics.
- [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/): Supports the manipulation, analysis, and visualization of tabular data.
- [Biopython](https://biopython.org/docs/latest/api/): Provides tools for biological sequence analysis and common bioinformatics file formats.
- [Pyrodigal](https://pyrodigal.readthedocs.io/en/stable/): Predicts protein-coding genes in prokaryotic genomes and metagenomes.
- [pysam](https://pysam.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): Reads and manipulates common genomics file formats such as SAM, BAM, and VCF.
- [sourmash](https://sourmash.readthedocs.io/en/stable/): Uses k-mers to compare genomes and analyse genomic or metagenomic datasets.
- [msprime](https://tskit.dev/msprime/docs/stable/) and [tskit](https://tskit.dev/tskit/docs/stable/): Simulate and analyse ancestry and genetic variation in populations.
- [FreeSASA](https://freesasa.github.io/python/): Calculates solvent-accessible surface areas for proteins and other molecular structures.
- [scikit-image](https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/): Provides image-processing algorithms useful for microscopy and other biological images.


## Technical details

JupyterLite is a WebAssembly (WASM) compiled version of the JupyterLab distribution, this means it runs in the browser on the client side - so there is no need for a server or any other complicated infrastructure.
